issues.body: fetch_bd_map records ambiguity independently per trust class, then apply_migration aborts on every touched ambiguous id. If a legitimate issue already has MIGRATION_LABEL, one marker-only copy is inert as intended, but two unprivileged marker-only issues with the same bd-id make the unverified class collide and put that id in ambiguous. The trusted issue is still canonical, so these decoys should remain inert; instead any user able to open two issues can stop --apply for that bead. This contradicts the stated threat-model rationale and is not exercised by the new tests.
issues.fix_hint: Exclude unverified-class collisions from ambiguous when the same bd-id has a trusted entry (or filter those collisions before aborting), while retaining trusted-class duplicate detection. Add a regression test with one MIGRATION_LABEL issue plus two marker-only copies and assert ambiguity is empty and apply_migration resumes the trusted issue.
issues.title: Two marker-only decoys can abort a trusted resume

verdict.summary: The new duplicate detection closes the arbitrary same-class selection case, but it introduces an unprivileged denial-of-service against otherwise canonical authenticated resumes. The implementation says marker-only copies of an authenticated issue are inert, yet two such copies are classified as ambiguous and abort --apply. The tests cover only one shadow copy, so they miss this security-relevant boundary.
